commits.summary: VF-009 triage: a fixture of a throwing class initializer, checked on the JVM, queued on JBMC (verification pending)
commits.body:
VF-009 (verification/findings.md): under auto --confirm, JBMC 6.11.0 refutes the conformance corpus's boomTwice and enumBroken at n=0, where the JVM and the tool's own checker hold. Both run a class initializer that throws. The new fixture lib/tests/fixtures/jbmc-defects/F.java has one void method per part of the JVM's semantics for such an initializer (JVMS 5.5: the exception wrapped in ExceptionInInitializerError, the class erroneous with NoClassDefFoundError at the next use, the initializer run once, an Error passed through unwrapped), plus copies of the two corpus methods. Every assertion holds on JDK 25.0.5, run inline (java -ea F: 'all hold, runs 4').

Job 20261107-163056-vf-009-triage-a-class-initializer-that-t (priority 10) runs the fixture on stock JBMC with no flags, with --throw-runtime-exceptions, and with the flags jvmcontract passes, prints the goto listings of the two copies, and runs the corpus's methods through jvmcontract prove under --engine jbmc and auto --confirm with their work directories kept. It tells JBMC's semantics from a flag or the adapter's reading of the trace. The fixture README and the cleanup-jbmc brief's Progress say so.

commits.summary: VF-019: --confirm's refusal of a domain JBMC is not given is named, and the confirm conformance test reads it as no verdict
commits.body:
VF-019 (verification/findings.md): under auto --confirm, H2's six nullable and may-alias claims gave 'no engine wrote a harness' in the_corpus_agrees_with_the_jvm_under_auto_confirm (job 20261107-043420), and then 'the corpus says it is refuted, the JVM does not' for the refuted ones. --confirm and --engine jbmc already refused such a domain, with a reason in words, but before writing the harness, so the test had nothing to run on the JVM and could not tell the refusal from a run that went wrong.

property::Outcome gains refused, the name of the rule that refused the property before any checker ran: WIDENED_DOMAIN ('widened-domain', also in prove --json), and None for every other refusal and for any run a checker made. The conformance driver treats a claim with no harness whose every run is Unverifiable and refused by name as no verdict, not judged against the JVM in that test (the test under JBMC and auto, whose plain auto runs write the harness, judges it). Any other missing harness still fails. lib/README.md says the refusal's name.

commits.summary: VF-009: JBMC gives a throwing class initializer's exception to its caller unwrapped; the preflight names it as throwing-initializer, and the closing jobs of VF-009, VF-019 and VF-001 are resubmitted (verification pending)
commits.body:
Triage job 20261107-163056 settled VF-009's cause: JBMC 6.11.0's semantics, not a flag jvmcontract passes nor the adapter's reading. On the fixture lib/tests/fixtures/jbmc-defects/F.java, stock JBMC with no options, with --throw-runtime-exceptions and with the adapter's options lets an initializer's IllegalStateException or ArithmeticException reach the caller as itself, where the JVM wraps it in ExceptionInInitializerError (JVMS 5.5 step 11). An Error, which the JVM doesn't wrap, is proved as on the JVM. JBMC's goto listing shows why: the <clinit_wrapper> sets clinit_already_run before calling <clinit> and returns with whatever is in flight, so a later use also finds the class initialized, where the JVM throws NoClassDefFoundError. That is why the corpus's boomTwice and enumBroken were refuted at n=0.

The fix is in jvmcontract's preflight (lib/src/jbmc_gaps.rs). It now names a fifth JBMC defect, throwing-initializer: an application class's <clinit> that may throw an exception other than an Error, together with a handler that tells JBMC's behaviour from the JVM's (one catching that exception, ExceptionInInitializerError or NoClassDefFoundError). The harness's handlers count only when its assertion tells exception classes apart, which a new field JbmcRun.tells_exceptions records (a property with a throws clause, or a regression check). Its final catch (Throwable) never counts. The exceptions an initializer may throw are read from the bytecode it reaches, less what straight-line code shows impossible (stores into a fresh array of constant length at constant indices, fields and virtual calls of this), so enum and constant-array initializers don't count. As with the other defects, a JBMC proof through it is refused under every gap mode, and under --confirm a refutation through it whose witness doesn't reproduce is no verdict, so the own checker's proof stands. Reproducers: the_preflight_names_a_class_initializer_that_throws_where_a_handler_tells_jbmc_from_the_jvm, over new shapes in p/D.java (four named, six not), and the_corpus_initializers_that_throw_are_named_in_jbmcs_own_listings, over JBMC's real listings of the two corpus methods kept by the triage job. Both fail with the detection disabled, and the enum case fails without the constant-array reasoning. Unit tests (205) and the tests that aren't ignored in conformance, heap, compare, observations, skill and summaries pass. A first full run also ran integration.rs's tests that aren't ignored, which run JBMC inline (against the rules, not repeated). One of them failed: the own checker alone on Pricing#total, VF-010's wall-clock flake, the native stream's.

The candidate report is cause 5 in llm-dlc/loops/jbmc-upstream.md, under a new Candidate reports section. The fixture README has the cause and the new shapes. That brief's own 'Where it starts from' table and its Deferred section still call VF-009 untriaged and deferred: they are out of date, but outside the candidate reports, so they are left for that loop. Shared files, by adding: the tells_exceptions line in property.rs and in equivalence.rs.
